sentence_stem: If I had studied harder at school,
correct_completion: I would have a better job now.
full_sentence: If I had studied harder at school, I would have a better job now.
acceptable_variants: I would be working in a better company now.

options.text: I will have a better job next year.
options.why_wrong: 'Will' belongs to the first conditional. It does not match the past perfect condition in the stem.

options.text: I had a better job last year.
options.why_wrong: The past simple describes a completed past situation. The stem needs a hypothetical present result with 'would'.

options.text: I would have a better job now.
I got a better job last year.
options.why_wrong: This is a real past event. It does not show the unreal present result of an unreal past condition.

grammar_focus: Mixed conditionals: past perfect in the if-clause, would + base verb for a present result
explanation: A mixed conditional links an unreal past condition with an unreal present result, so the main clause uses 'would' plus a base verb with a present time reference. Spanish speakers may use the same tense in both clauses because Spanish marks this idea with a different verb form, so English needs the past perfect in the if-clause and a would-form in the result.
translation: Si hubiera estudiado más en la escuela, ahora tendría un mejor trabajo.
